messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired: GPU_MEMORY_PRESSURE (pool=gpu-pool-eu1) severity=high - 6 active alerts
pagerduty: PagerDuty alert -> assignment: annika (oncall) · incident key: pd-98765
annika: Acked. looking at recent deploys + redispatch logs. committing to 15m initial triage window :hourglass_flowing_sand:
leo: saw a burst of kvcache evictions around the same time, might be prefetch thrash. grabbing nvml dumps now
annika: thanks. can you paste the nvml summary here when ready?
leo: paste:```GPU0: 15GB total, 14.2GB used, processes: 3
- pid 4123 (redwood-infer): 9.8GB
- pid 4987 (redwood-kv): 3.6GB
- pid 6781 (probe): 200MB
OOM events: 0 in last 30m, mem_pressure spikes at 2m intervals```
annika: interesting — no hard OOM but sustained pressure + reclaim loop. check autoscaler behavior?
kevin: autoscaler shows pool capacity stable; no scale-up because CPU headroom low. looks like kernel reclaim on GPU is kicking in rather than process OOMs
annika: running a quick mitigation: marking problematic nodes unsched for inference, draining active low-priority pods. command: `kubectl cordon gpu-eu1-node-23 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-eu1-node-23`
incident-bot: Action recorded: node cordoned/drain started by annika
julie: support: we're seeing a small bump in customer 503s in EU region, ~2 customers impacted intermittently, affected endpoints: /v1/generate. informing customers now
annika: thanks julie — note customer impact in the incident ticket. I'll also enable fallback routing to cpu-fallback pool for high-latency requests: `route update --from gpu-pool-eu1 --to cpu-fallback --condition latency>1200ms` (will monitor for cost impact)
pagerduty: PagerDuty escalation: alert retriggered and unacked for 5m, escalating to kevin
kevin: Taking handoff — I'm on it. reviewing kernel logs and host-side cgroup throttles
kevin: found repeated cudaErrorMemoryAllocation traces in host logs correlated with prefetch spikes, working hypothesis: aggressive kv-prefetch + long sequences saturating memory windows
leo: can we temporarily reduce prefetch concurrency? patch suggestion: `KV_PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=2` and bump kvcache eviction threshold to 0.85
annika: rolling that change to staging now, will push to canary in prod after 2 min smoke test
annika: smoke canary ok on 2 nodes, applying to remaining pools with 30s stagger
incident-bot: Change applied: KV_PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=2 · rollout id roll-2026-03-17-01
pagerduty: PagerDuty note: alert acknowledged by kevin; remaining alerts showing decreasing severity
julie: support update: customer 503s reduced, no new reports in the last 10m. sending follow-up email to impacted customers now :email:
kevin: monitoring telemetry — GPU memory headroom recovered to ~1.2GB across pool, evictions down by 70%
annika: nice. I'll leave a short-term mitigation playbook in the ticket and handoff to kevin for the 1h watch. created INC-2026-03017 in Jira with steps, logs attached
kevin: taking over on-call watch. annika — if you need to step off, ping me, otherwise I'll continue monitoring and start a postmortem if we see recurrence
annika: stepping off now. good job team. :thumbsup:
kevin: noted. will rotate to next oncall in 45m if stable. closing PD alert once stable window reaches 30m
incident-bot: PD alert closed by kevin after stable window
julie: will draft customer postmortem summary with the mitigation notes and timeline
kevin: FYI I'll run a deeper heaptrace/alloc profile tomorrow and propose longer-term fixes (backpressure on prefetch + smarter kvcache sizing)
annika: thanks — add eval tests for long-sequence flows to avoid regressions
leo: adding perf test to bench infra (kvcache + long prompts)
kevin: logged followups: #1 reduce default prefetch concurrency; #2 add guardrail to autoscaler for GPU pools to allow short burst scale-ups; #3 alert tuning to reduce flapping.
julie: INC-2026-03017 updated with customer comms draft
kevin: closing thread here — will update Jira with final notes after watch window.
